newsitem.title: POLAND: FORECAST - Higher Polish trade gap, CPI in Dec-Feb.
newsitem.headline: FORECAST - Higher Polish trade gap, CPI in Dec-Feb.

text.p: Following is a monthly macroeconomic forecast prepared for Reuters by the Planning Ministry's (CUP) chief analyst Tadeusz Chroscicki.
The forecast gives predictions for key indicators for three months in advance.

The trade deficit is growing fast and for the whole of 1996 it could exceed $8 billion aginst $1.8 billion in 1995. In the first two months of next year the trade gap can reach about $1.5 billion and will be about 30 percent higher than in the same period of last year. @
In December consumer prices are expected to grow at a slightly higher rate than in November and year-on-year inflation at the end of the year is likely to reach almost 19 percent.

The first quarter of 1997 will be characterised by faster growth in consumer prices because of several increases of government controlled prices of electricity, heating gas and water as well as of insurance premiums. @

A significant inflationary pressure will be also felt from high wage growth in the enterprise sector in the last quarter of this year, high consumer credit expansion and a declining household propensity to save.

NOTE: The forecast revised up 1996 trade deficit forecast to $8.1 billion from $7.3 billion predicted in November. It also increased inflation forecasts for year-end and January to 18.9 percent and 2.7 percent respectively from earlier predicted 18.7 percent and two percent. @
